subject: Consortium: evidence handoff & notification alignment
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finconsortium.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Ops <security@finconsortium.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: cross-org evidence handoff expectations and notification timing

Hi Jonas,

Quick intro — I'm Alice on FinConsortium's Legal & Security ops. We're aligning an interbank consortium playbook for incident cooperation and want to confirm Redwood's approach to evidence handoffs and notification timelines. A few specific asks:

- If a telemetry/ingestion-related exposure is suspected, what is Redwood's standard notification window for customers and partners? Do you operate on 48h/72h timelines and what triggers each?
- Can you provide a short list of what you can deliver for forensic handoff (raw telemetry, KV cache snapshots, per-request traces, TLS-meta) and expected time-to-export?
- How do you coordinate when a subprocessor (e.g., managed hosting or telemetry aggregator) is involved — who owns the chain-of-custody and who signs the export?

We have a tight board timeline and would appreciate an example handoff checklist plus any gating questions that would delay export (e.g., legal holds, cross-border encryption issues).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

Best,
Alice Chen
Legal & Security Ops | FinConsortium
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finconsortium.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-30T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: cross-org evidence handoff expectations and notification timing

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (LegalOps lead) and Ben (Platform SRE) so we can provide concrete artifacts. High level:

- Notification timing: our baseline DPA sets a 72-hour notification "target" for confirmed incidents that materially affect customer data; we also have an internal rapid-alert path (within 24 hours) to affected customers for critical exfiltration indicators when forensic evidence is available. The difference is confirmed vs suspected events and whether forensic exports are needed immediately.

- Evidence we can provide: per-request traces (redacted PII), KV cache snapshot exports (timeboxed), sampling of telemetry (ingestion logs), and a forensic runtime snapshot. For cross-border exports we provide encrypted archives; keys are managed through customer KMS integrations when applicable.

- Subprocessor coordination: we operate an outbound request model — if a subprocessor holds relevant artifacts we will coordinate authorization and a signed chain-of-custody. Typically Redwood takes custody of the exported artifacts and produces a signed transfer manifest; if the subprocessor must export directly we require a co-signed manifest and an attestation from them.

I'll attach our internal evidence-handoff checklist and a sample forensic snapshot request template; Ben, please confirm export lead times and any known blockers.

Jonas Weber
Head of Privacy Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finconsortium.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: cross-org evidence handoff expectations and notification timing

Attaching the export ETA table — rough estimates below for planning:

- Per-request traces (sanitized): 2-6 hours after signed request + custodian approval
- Telemetry sample (compressed tar): 6-24 hours
- KV cache snapshot (timeboxed): 24-36 hours (requires runtime freeze for chosen shard)
- Full forensic runtime snapshot (VM image + kernel logs): 48-96 hours depending on cluster schedule and subprocessor involvement

Blockers to watch for: legal holds, ongoing active mitigation (we won't snapshot mid-containment unless customer authorizes), and HSM/KMS key escrow constraints for cross-border encrypted exports. If FinConsortium requires the keys, we can arrange an HSM-backed transfer with a short-lived key and audit logs.

I've uploaded the ETA table and the forensic-snapshot-request.xlsx to the Drive link Jonas included. Also attached a sanitized telemetry sample for your review.

Attachments: forensic-snapshot-request.xlsx (see Drive), telemetry-sample-logs.tar.gz

—Ben
SRE Manager, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finconsortium.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-03T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: cross-org evidence handoff expectations and notification timing

Alice — adding legal context. A few clarifications to avoid mismatched expectations:

- DPA thresholds vs. operational alerts: Our DPA language defines incident "notification" as an obligation once an event is reasonably likely to affect confidentiality or integrity of customer data. That is contract-level; operationally we may notify earlier for triage. We should confirm which standard the consortium prefers for public-facing notices.

- 72h vs. 48h: We cannot guarantee a 48h public notification in every case due to required forensic verification and potential cross-border approvals; we can commit to an internal 24h rapid-alert for partners and a 72h window for escalated, confirmed notices. If FinConsortium needs a firm 48h SLA we will need to add it as a DPA amendment or an SLA addendum.

- Subprocessor delegation: Redwood will provide the transfer manifest and co-sign attestation when feasible. If a subprocessor (e.g., telemetry aggregator) is non-cooperative or subject to local law preventing export, we'll provide alternative evidence (redacted traces, aggregated telemetry, and signed attestations) and document the legal basis.

Action items for us:
1) Jonas/Ben: finalize the evidence-handoff-checklist PDF and attach the ETA table.
2) Kimberly: draft a short DPA amendment language around 48h public notice vs 72h confirmed notice.
3) Alice: confirm whether the consortium wants a signed chain-of-custody template or if a co-signed attestation is sufficient.

Marissa Cole
Legal Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finconsortium.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Ops <security@finconsortium.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: cross-org evidence handoff expectations and notification timing

Marissa/Jonas — this is very helpful, thank you. Consortium response: we prefer a primary model where Redwood provides a co-signed chain-of-custody manifest plus the artifacts listed as standard (sanitized traces, telemetry sample, KV snapshot). For public-facing notices we will accept 72h by default but are asking members to adopt a 48h target for consumer-facing markets; we understand an SLA amendment may be required.

For the immediate board ask, please send the finalized checklist and the forensic request template (we'll use the DocuSign link to accept the attestation). On the co-signed manifest: a simple signed transfer manifest (PDF) is sufficient; if subprocessor exports are required we request the subprocessor attestation and an explanation of any legal/evidentiary gaps.

We'll schedule a 30m sync next week to finalize the addendum language. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Legal & Security Ops | FinConsortium
